{{short description|American mathematics educator|bot=PearBOT 5}}
{{family name hatnote|Civil||lang=Spanish}}
'''Marta Civil''' is an American [[mathematics education|mathematics educator]]. Her research involves understanding the cultural background of minority schoolchildren, particularly [[Hispanic and Latino Americans|Hispanic and Latina/o]] students in the [[Southwestern United States]], and using that understanding to promote parent engagement and focus mathematics teaching on  students' individual strengths.{{r|fsmc|the74|personal}} She is the Roy F. Graesser Endowed Professor at the [[University of Arizona]], where she holds appointments in the department of mathematics, the department of mathematics education, and the department of teaching, learning, and sociocultural studies.{{r|pmena}}

==Education and career==
Civil earned her Ph.D. at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]] in 1990. Her dissertation, ''Doing and Talking about Mathematics: A Study of Preservice Elementary Teachers'', was supervised by Peter George Braunfeld.{{r|mgp}} In 2011 she moved from the University of Arizona to the [[University of North Carolina]], to become Frank A. Daniels Distinguished Professor of Mathematics Education,{{r|fsmc}} but returned to Arizona in 2014 to become the Graesser Professor.{{r|personal}}

==Books==
Civil is co-editor of the books ''Transnational and Borderland Studies in Mathematics Education'' (Routledge, 2011),{{r|tbs}} ''Latinos/as and Mathematics Education: Research on Learning and Teaching in Classrooms and Communities'' (Information Age, 2011),{{r|lme}} ''Cases for Mathematics Teacher Educators: Facilitating Conversations about Inequities in Mathematics Classrooms'' (Information Age, 2016),{{r|cases}} and ''Access & Equity: Promoting High-Quality Mathematics in Grades 3-5'' (National Council of Teachers of Mathematics, 2018).{{r|ae}}

==Recognition==
In 2013 TODOS: Mathematics for All gave Civil their Iris M. Carl Equity and Leadership Award.{{r|carl}}
She is included in a deck of playing cards featuring notable women mathematicians published by the Association of Women in Mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mathematicians of EvenQuads Deck 1 |url=https://awm-math.org/publications/playing-cards/deck1/#civil |access-date=2022-06-18 |website=awm-math.org}}</ref> She received the 2021 [[National Council of Teachers of Mathematics]] (NCTM) Lifetime Achievement Award.<ref name="NCTM Lifetime Achievement">{{cite web | title=2021 Lifetime Achievement Award Recipient Marta Civil | website=nctm.org | url=https://www.nctm.org/Grants-and-Awards/Lifetime-Achievement-Award/Marta-Civil/ | access-date=3 Dec 2022}}</ref>
